blindSummary:
This state/province's religious penal code took effect 31 January 2001 and prescribes stoning to death for married or previously married offenders convicted of consensual same-sex sexual activity (100 lashes where unmarried), with discretionary punishment (up to 100 lashes and/or imprisonment) extending to same-sex acts between women and to cases involving a minor - the most capital-heavy statutory text within the twelve-state religious-law belt. Religious-morality police activity is documented here. A foreign government's religious-freedom commission's 2019 case-level study covers this state among the three belt states sampled (173 religious-court cases, 2017).

The explicit death-by-stoning text combined with sampled case evidence distinguishes this unit alongside another belt state that pairs capital text with the most active morality-police force; one further belt state has a carried-out stoning sentence on record.
